metaTitle: Research — Diagnostic AI & Precision Diagnostics | Candice Chu
metaDescription: Three research pillars: diagnostic AI and digital cytology, large language models and veterinary informatics, and molecular biomarkers for kidney disease.
intro: The lab develops and evaluates artificial intelligence for veterinary diagnostics, builds the informatics that makes clinical data usable, and pursues molecular biomarkers for earlier disease detection.

quote.text: Our goal is to integrate AI into veterinary diagnostics while educating the next generation of veterinarians.

fundingNote: Award amounts, grant numbers and collaborator lists are intentionally not published. Sponsor names, project titles, role and status are shown; anything awaiting an official project title is held back until confirmed.

pillars.title: Diagnostic AI and Digital Cytology
pillars.overview: Building and validating computer-vision models on clinically curated, specialist-annotated veterinary image datasets — with attention to diagnostic performance, error analysis, and what it actually takes to deploy a model in a diagnostic laboratory.

cards.title: AI-Assisted Canine Lymphoma Cytology
cards.description: Detection and classification of neutrophils and small, intermediate and large lymphocytes across 680 cytology images with 25,761 specialist-annotated cells. Work spans image acquisition, annotation, a YOLO detection workflow, diagnostic performance and error analysis.

image.alt: Study workflow: case identification, image acquisition and quality control, cell annotation, data splitting with five-fold cross-device validation, and model performance

cards.title: AI for Canine Hip Dysplasia Screening
cards.description: Convolutional neural networks for hip dysplasia severity grading across 22,482 canine hip radiographs, with translational relevance to human orthopedic screening. Supported by the Orthopedic Foundation for Animals in collaboration with UT Southwestern Medical Center.

cards.title: AI for Canine Pancreatitis Diagnosis and Prognosis
cards.description: Neural networks, logistic regression and gradient-boosted models applied to 1,384 suspected canine pancreatitis cases for diagnosis and prognostication.

image.alt: Illustration of a dog with the pancreas highlighted

cards.title: AI for Bile Cytology Interpretation

pillars.title: Large Language Models and Veterinary Informatics
pillars.description: Clinical records · AI scribes · Evaluation & governance
pillars.overview: Turning free-text veterinary records into structured, research-ready data — and measuring where language models fail. Evaluation, hallucination and error analysis, and data governance are treated as first-class research questions, not afterthoughts.

cards.title: AI Scribe Evaluation for Clinical Documentation
cards.description: Evaluating AI scribe tools in veterinary clinical workflows: documentation burden, accuracy of generated records, and the review process a clinician still needs to own. Supported by VetRec.

cards.title: Dog Aging Project: Large-Scale Clinical Data Extraction
cards.description: Prompt-driven extraction of structured clinical variables from roughly 50,000 veterinary medical records contributed to the Dog Aging Project.

pillars.title: Molecular and Precision Diagnostics
pillars.overview: Non-invasive molecular markers for kidney disease in dogs and cats, built on RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics and digital cytometry — and read across to human nephrology wherever the biology allows.

cards.title: Urinary Extracellular Vesicle microRNAs in Feline CKD
cards.description: Identifying urinary extracellular vesicle-derived microRNAs as sensitive and specific biomarkers for early-stage feline chronic kidney disease. Supported by the EveryCat Health Foundation.

cards.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing and Digital Cytometry of the Canine Kidney
cards.description: Single-cell atlases of the canine kidney that enable digital cytometry — estimating cell-type composition from bulk transcriptomes and tracking how it shifts as chronic kidney disease progresses.
